purpose: Test that the selector improves method choice when a label-free feature truly changes the best method, while retaining a no-signal safety check.
claim_boundary: This is a software and construct-validity experiment. It is not biological validation and cannot support a personalised-superiority claim on real studies.
repair_reason: The v3 success predicate was logically impossible because coverage meant choosing a non-global method while success also required the global method among covered units.

model.family: multi-output ridge method-score regression with alpha fixed at 1.0
model.features: one independent switch feature plus eight independent noise features
model.threshold_semantics: minimum predicted method-score gain over the training-derived global method
model.calibration_rule: Among thresholds with signal-calibration coverage at least 0.20, signal point deployed regret below always-global, signal upper 95% paired-bootstrap bound at most 0.02, and null-calibration upper bound at most 0.02, choose highest signal coverage; break ties by lower signal deployed regret then higher threshold.

signal_test_success.deployed_regret_superiority: upper 95% paired-bootstrap bound of selector minus always-global regret is below zero

null_test_success.data_generating_rule: The training-derived global method is uniformly best; the switch feature is fixed at zero and contains no local method-switch information.
null_test_success.deployed_regret_noninferiority: upper 95% paired-bootstrap bound of selector minus always-global regret is at most 0.02
